items.title: REDEEM
items.full_name: Resilience in Desertification and Drought for Mediterranean
items.summary: Leading an expert team supporting Montenegro’s Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management in REDEEM, connecting WEFE nexus analysis, stakeholder engagement, integrated water governance, carbon footprint assessment and capacity building.
items.role: Key Expert — Team Leader, WEFE Nexus and Water Governance Expert, Montenegro
items.body:
Programme: Interreg Euro-MED 2021–2027

REDEEM addresses water scarcity, drought and ecosystem degradation in Mediterranean rural areas through an integrated Water–Energy–Food–Ecosystems (WEFE) nexus approach. It connects evidence, governance and practical solutions to strengthen water resilience and support more sustainable resource use.
items.contribution:
Contracted by: E3 Consulting, Podgorica, Montenegro
Beneficiary institution: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management of Montenegro (MAFWM)
Geographical coverage: Montenegro

As Key Expert and Team Leader within E3 Consulting’s support to Montenegro’s Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management (MAFWM), I coordinate technical delivery, integrate specialist contributions and serve as the principal operational interface with the Ministry. My role combines WEFE nexus and water governance expertise with responsibility for methodology, stakeholder engagement, quality assurance and reporting.

The assignment supports the mapping of Montenegro’s territorial WEFE nexus, stakeholder surveys and the analysis of barriers to adopting water-efficient solutions. It also contributes to institutional learning, policy recommendations and coordination among organisations responsible for water, energy, agriculture and ecosystems.

Support to pilot demonstration and resilience planning includes technical and governance inputs linked to solar-powered drip irrigation, the assessment and transfer of pilot findings, and the development of a territorial water resilience plan through a Local Working Group. This work aims to connect practical solutions with institutional responsibilities, end-user needs and wider opportunities for replication.

The assignment also covers carbon footprint assessment, including relevant Scope 3 emissions, and greenhouse gas mitigation planning. Capacity-building resources, stakeholder workshops, policy-transfer activities and digital learning materials help translate analytical findings into practical knowledge and action.

Throughout the contract, I will oversee task dependencies, coordinate expert inputs and review the consistency and technical quality of deliverables. My contribution helps connect project requirements with evidence-based analysis, inclusive dialogue and practical implementation in Montenegro.
items.results:
Progress to date (October 19, 2026)

  • Prepared and submitted Inception report

  • Organized Kick off meeting with beneficiary institution

  • Developed full Project work plan and digital repository

items.title: SATECON
items.summary: Providing strategic advice on blue–green innovation and collaboration platforms within SATECON, connecting policy, digital technologies and institutional capacity to support sustainable agriculture, mariculture and cross-border cooperation.
items.role: Senior Advisor for Blue–Green Innovation and Collaboration Platforms
items.body:
Programme: Interreg VI-A IPA Croatia–Bosnia and Herzegovina–Montenegro 2021–2027

SATECON promotes smart, innovative and sustainable agriculture across Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Montenegro. Through digitalisation, pilot actions and cross-border knowledge transfer, the project connects research institutions, public authorities and SMEs to strengthen innovation ecosystems and sustainable value chains in agriculture and mariculture.
items.contribution:
Contracted by: Institute of Marine Biology, University of Montenegro
Geographical coverage: Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Montenegro

As Senior Advisor for Blue–Green Innovation and Collaboration Platforms, I support the alignment of project activities with relevant policies, institutional priorities and Programme requirements. My work combines strategic advice, platform development, quality assurance and capacity building.

Strategic advice and policy alignment
I review project work plans, deliverables and governance arrangements, examining their links to EU, regional and national policy frameworks, including the Green Deal, Smart Specialisation and blue economy policies. Strategic advisory notes provide recommendations on implementation progress, policy alignment, optimisation and risk mitigation. The assignment also includes support to institutional strategies and a final position paper on blue–green innovation and collaboration platforms.

Collaboration platforms and innovation ecosystems
I review concepts, prototypes and outputs related to digital collaboration platforms, innovation clusters and advisory tools. My advice addresses governance, long-term sustainability, user roles, interoperability and cross-border relevance, helping connect technical development with institutional responsibilities and user needs.

Reporting and quality assurance
I prepare narrative partner progress reports and review deliverables for clarity, consistency, accuracy and supporting evidence. This work helps maintain alignment between activities, indicators, reported achievements and Programme requirements throughout implementation and closure.

Coordination and capacity building
Working with the Project Manager and institutional teams, I support stakeholder consultations, project meetings and expert discussions. I also mentor staff involved in innovation management, digital platform development and reporting, helping strengthen the capacity needed to sustain project results.
items.results:
Progress to date (October 19, 2026)

  • Facilitated project team meetings in Montenegro

  • Contributed to Deliverable D.1.1.1 Report on agricultural existing regulatory and legislative framework across Cro, B&H and Mne

  • Contributed to Deliverable D.3.1.1 SATECON Blueprint for Smart Agriculture Solutions: Tailored Technological Packages

items.title: BLUECONNECT
items.full_name: Enhancing Cross-Border Blue Growth: Fostering Innovation and Cooperation for Competitive Entrepreneurship
items.image_alt: BLUECONNECT project team meeting 23 September 2026: Branka Pestorioc (left), Radoje Laušević (right)
items.summary: Providing expert support for the development and long-term sustainability of the Blue Growth Collaboration Platform (BGCP), strengthening cross-border knowledge exchange, innovation and cooperation.
items.body: BLUECONNECT strengthens cross-border cooperation between research institutions and business organisations in Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Montenegro to advance a sustainable and competitive blue economy. The project supports research, innovation and technology uptake through a Blue Growth Cluster and an online collaboration platform connecting businesses, researchers and public authorities. Three pilot initiatives address aquaculture management, fisheries monitoring and resource-efficient freshwater fish processing, translating scientific knowledge into practical solutions. By promoting knowledge exchange, circular economy practices and more efficient use of aquatic resources, BLUECONNECT aims to strengthen entrepreneurship, improve environmental performance and support the long-term resilience of coastal and freshwater-based economies. Visit project photo gallery: LINK.
items.contribution:
Programme: Interreg IPA Croatia–Bosnia and Herzegovina–Montenegro 2021–2027
Contracted by: Institute of Marine Biology, University of Montenegro
Geographical coverage: Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro

Providing expert support for the development and long-term sustainability of the Blue Growth Collaboration Platform (BGCP), strengthening cross-border knowledge exchange, innovation and cooperation among businesses, research institutions and public authorities.

My responsibilities include:

  • Digital platform development: Preparing Terms of Reference for software development and coordinating with IT experts on platform design, development and launch; incorporating stakeholder feedback to ensure usability and effective communication, knowledge exchange and networking.

  • Regional cluster development: Working with the Regional Blue Growth Cluster Expert to connect businesses, research centres and other relevant organisations; organising networking events, workshops and collaborative activities that support innovation, entrepreneurship and cluster sustainability.

  • Partnership and governance: Leading the preparation and negotiation of partnership and cooperation agreements; developing arrangements for continued platform and cluster management, with clear partner roles, responsibilities and decision-making processes.

  • Stakeholder engagement: Mapping and engaging local and regional stakeholders; facilitating meetings, workshops and consultations to gather input and align platform development with users’ needs and evolving priorities.

  • Monitoring and reporting: Developing monitoring tools, tracking implementation against project objectives and timelines, preparing progress reports, and recommending corrective measures to address challenges and delays.

  • Communication and dissemination: Developing and implementing a communication plan; coordinating outreach through digital channels, newsletters and events to increase platform visibility, stakeholder participation and opportunities for cooperation across the blue economy.
items.results:
Progress to date (October 19, 2026)

  • Developed digital platform https://adriaticbgc.org/

  • Developed Adriatic Blue Growth Cluster

  • Drafted partnership and cooperation agreements

  • Supported workshops and project team meetings

items.title: AZA4ICE
items.full_name: Allocated Zones for Circular Aquaculture to Trigger the Transition to an Inclusive Circular Economy
items.image_alt: Dr. Radoje Laušević speaking on LiRRIE event in Ulcinj, Montenegro on 4th March 2025
items.summary: Provided expert support in Montenegro to the Chamber of Commerce of Montenegro within AZA4ICE, co-funded by the European Union through the Interreg Euro-MED Programme 2021–2027.
items.role: Expert in Living Responsible Research and Innovation Ecosystems (LiRRIEs) and Inclusive Circular Economy (ICE)
items.body:
Programme: Interreg Euro-MED Programme 2021–2027
AZA4ICE project combined spatial planning, stakeholder participation and circular business models to advance sustainable aquaculture in coastal and inland waters, including the Šasko Lake pilot area. Visit project photo gallery: LINK.
items.contribution:
Contracted by: Chamber of Commerce of Montenegro
Geographical scope: Montenegro

My responsibilities included:

  • Stakeholder mapping and engagement: Mapping quintuple-helix stakeholders representing education, business, environmental interests, civil society/media and public authorities; analysing challenges and opportunities for circular aquaculture.

  • LiRRIE development and facilitation: Supporting the development of a shared vision and establishment of the LiRRIE Forum; organising and moderating participatory events to inform the co-creation of Allocated Zones for Circular Aquaculture (C-AZA).

  • Circular economy assessment: Collecting and documenting circular aquaculture practices and business models, identifying business opportunities, and reviewing relevant legal and regulatory frameworks.

  • Action planning: Supporting the development of Montenegro’s action plan for an inclusive and circular aquaculture sector, incorporating stakeholder feedback and alignment with Smart Specialisation Strategies (S3).

  • Institutional cooperation and transfer: Facilitating stakeholder engagement for Memoranda of Understanding and preparing a transfer plan to support the uptake, adaptation and institutional integration of project results.

  • Awareness and learning: Providing stakeholder-informed inputs for the AZA4ICE educational board game and comic book.
items.results:
• Helped establish and operationalise Montenegro’s Living Responsible Research and Innovation Ecosystem (LiRRIE) for circular aquaculture at Šasko Lake through quintuple-helix stakeholder mapping, analysis of sector challenges and opportunities, and a jointly agreed development vision.

  • Secured Declarations of Participation from six organisations, supporting the launch and operation of the LiRRIE stakeholder forum.

  • Supported four consultation and training events, moderated stakeholder discussions, and delivered training on circular aquaculture and business transformation, including application of the BLUEfasma circularity self-assessment tool.

  • Prepared the stakeholder evaluation report on the AZA4ICE methodology and Allocated Zones for Circular Aquaculture (C-AZA), documenting and analysing feedback from public authorities, businesses and citizens.

  • Compiled circular aquaculture business practices, business opportunities and support mechanisms, and developed educational and training materials.

  • Prepared Montenegro’s Circular Aquaculture Action Plan, translating scientific findings and stakeholder priorities into six coordinated actions: capacity building; a proposed freshwater Integrated Multi-Trophic Aquaculture (IMTA) demonstration pilot; community circularity initiatives; environmental monitoring and safeguards; business support and financing; and inclusive governance.

  • Prepared the final LiRRIE report, consolidating consultation outcomes, stakeholder evaluations and lessons learned, and facilitated Memoranda of Understanding supporting continued cooperation and future implementation.

  • Developed Montenegro’s transferability plan, identifying opportunities, enabling conditions and practical pathways for replicating AZA4ICE methodologies, tools and governance approaches in other territories and sectors.

items.title: TOUR
items.image_alt: TOUR project team members in Lovćen National Park, Montenegro, end station of Kotor Cable Car
items.summary: Supported sustainable tourism and nature conservation in Montenegro through stakeholder engagement, workshops and cross-border cooperation within the South Adriatic region.
items.body: TOUR strengthened cross-border cooperation between Italy, Albania and Montenegro to promote environmentally responsible tourism in the South Adriatic. Funded by the Interreg IPA South Adriatic Programme 2021–2027, the project helped public authorities, tourism operators and local communities identify practical approaches to ecotourism and address pressures associated with overcrowding, seasonality and tourism development. Through workshops, business exchanges, stakeholder consultations and conferences, the four partners developed a shared ecotourism strategy and Joint Action Plan. These outputs connected environmental conservation, cultural heritage and local economic opportunities, providing a framework for more sustainable destination management and continued cross-border cooperation. Visit photo gallery: LINK.
items.contribution:
Contracted by: Tourism Organisation of Kotor
Geographical scope: Montenegro

As Tourism and Conservation Specialist I provided expert support for activities addressing tourism’s influence on natural landscapes in Montenegro. The assignment covered the preparation, facilitation and reporting of an ecotourism workshop, coordination of an incoming mission exploring ecotourism business opportunities and conservation practices, and preparation of a conference on responsible relationships with the environment. Responsibilities included developing supporting event toolkits, engaging project partners and local stakeholders, and contributing to progress and activity reports.
items.results:
• Joint ecotourism strategy: Developed a shared framework for sustainable tourism governance, certification, green infrastructure, community participation and environmental education.

  • Territorial needs assessment: Collected and analysed 54 questionnaires across Italy, Albania and Montenegro, identifying common constraints, territorial strengths and priorities for ecotourism development.

  • Joint Action Plan: Consolidated territorial analyses and national contributions into a cross-border framework covering strategic priorities, implementation arrangements, monitoring and replication.

  • Stakeholder validation: Tested and refined the proposed approaches through the international conference “Responsible Relationship with the Environment” in Kotor on 20 May 2025, using three territorial working groups and interactive stakeholder voting.

  • Montenegro’s contribution: Integrated proposals addressing visitor management, institutional coordination, inland tourism development and digital tools, alongside a proposed action-plan structure and partner evaluation questionnaire.

  • Continued cooperation: Formalised the four partners’ commitment through a Memorandum of Understanding supporting implementation, dissemination and further development of the joint methodology beyond the project.

items.title: SKILLS
items.full_name: High LEVEL and market-respondent Competences for a Blue and Digitalized “Smart and skilled South Adriatic”
items.image_alt: Dr Radoje Laušević speaking on the SKILLS meeting
items.summary: Provided expertise in policy analysis, stakeholder engagement, communication, and monitoring and evaluation for SKILLS, supporting cross-border cooperation and the development of skills aligned with the needs of the South Adriatic blue economy.
items.role: Expert in Policy Analysis, Stakeholder Engagement, Communication and Monitoring & Evaluation
items.body:
Programme: Interreg IPA South Adriatic 2021–2027

SKILLS strengthens cross-border cooperation between institutions, education and training providers, and businesses in Albania, Italy and Montenegro to develop a skilled and competitive blue economy in the South Adriatic. Guided by employers’ needs and labour market trends, the project improves educational pathways, develops new learning programmes and tests on-the-job training schemes to address shortages of blue and digital skills. Its activities support young people and students entering blue careers, while helping enterprises strengthen workforce competencies and human resource management. Through a shared cross-border strategy, coordinated qualification frameworks, a Adriatic Blue Growth Cluster and a digital platform, SKILLS connects education, policy and industry to improve employment opportunities, support innovation and advance sustainable regional growth.
items.contribution:
Contracted by: University of Montenegro — Institute of Marine Biology, Lead Partner
Geographical coverage: South Adriatic cross-border area — Montenegro, Albania, and the Italian regions of Puglia and Molise

My assignment combined policy analysis, stakeholder engagement, communication, and monitoring and evaluation. I supported cooperation among institutions, education providers, research organisations and businesses, helping connect sector priorities with the project’s skills-development objectives.

The policy and stakeholder-engagement work focused on understanding institutional perspectives, identifying development and training needs, and supporting dialogue across sectors and borders. This approach helped establish a shared understanding of the challenges facing the blue economy and the opportunities for coordinated action.

Communication and monitoring support complemented this work by making project objectives and activities accessible to stakeholders and supporting the systematic review of implementation progress. My contribution linked evidence, participation and communication to practical project delivery, providing a basis for informed decisions and continued cooperation.
items.results:
• Contributed to establishing cross-border governance and stakeholder engagement foundations for blue economy skills development in the South Adriatic.

  • Supported the launch of the Cross-Border Permanent Table (CBPT) through its inaugural meeting in Bari on 4 October 2024.

  • Contributed to completing Montenegro’s 4-Helix Stakeholder Engagement Report, mapping academia, industry, public authorities and civil society, identifying cooperation gaps, and documenting Montenegro’s appointed CBPT members.

  • Supported three Skills Definition Labs in Montenegro: Most Needed Blue Economy Skills (Podgorica, 19 November 2024); Aquaculture and Fisheries Management (Kotor, 27 November 2024); and Maritime Logistics and Port Management (Tivat, 13 December 2024).

  • Helped identify workforce gaps and formulate recommendations for tailored training programmes and closer alignment between education and industry needs through these stakeholder consultations.

items.title: SECAP
items.full_name: EU4 Energy Transition: Covenant of Mayors in the Western Balkans and Türkiye (EU4ETTR)
items.summary: Supported the development of Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plans (SECAPs) for selected local self-government units in the Western Balkans through leadership of the country expert team.
items.body:
The project supports municipalities in the Western Balkans in developing and implementing Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plans (SECAPs), helping translate EU energy and climate objectives into practical local measures. Implemented within GIZ’s Open Regional Fund for South-East Europe – Energy, Transport and Climate Protection, and supported through the EU4Energy Transition initiative*, it strengthens municipal capacity for coordinated energy planning, decarbonisation and climate resilience under the Covenant of Mayors framework. By promoting regional cooperation, knowledge exchange and stronger institutional capabilities, the project helps local authorities address implementation gaps, align local policies with EU standards and advance sustainable urban development. The broader programme is co-funded by the European Union and the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).

*The EU4 Energy Transition: Covenant of Mayors in the Western Balkans and Türkiye (EU4ETTR) project supported local governments in reducing carbon emissions, addressing climate change and transitioning to clean, sustainable energy. Running from March 2021 to February 2025, with final conferences held on May 28, 2025, the initiative had a total budget of €9.335 million, comprising €8 million from the European Union and €1.335 million from Germany’s BMZ. It covered six Western Balkan economies and Türkiye, with implementation led by GIZ in the Western Balkans and Lithuania’s Central Project Management Agency (CPMA) in Türkiye.
items.contribution:
Commissioned by: ibf expertise, Brussels, Belgium, under its contract with GIZ
Geographical coverage: Serbia
Expert input: 25 working days

Supported the development of Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plans (SECAPs) for selected local self-government units in the Western Balkans through leadership of the country expert team.

Led the country expert team responsible for supporting SECAP preparation in 4 municipalities in Serbia: Novi Sad, Pirot, Valjevo, and Vranje. Coordinating expert contributions to local sustainable energy and climate action planning. The assignment comprised 25 working days of expert input.
items.results:
• Led and coordinated the country expert team’s contribution to four Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plans (SECAPs) in Serbia.

  • Novi Sad SECAP — March 2024: Supported the development of an integrated plan addressing climate change mitigation, resilience and equitable access to sustainable energy, underpinned by stakeholder participation and cooperation. Official document: Акциони план за одрживу енергију и климу (SECAP) за Град Нови Сад

  • Pirot SECAP — May 2024: Supported the development of a plan combining greenhouse gas emission reduction, climate adaptation and measures addressing energy poverty, with emphasis on affordable energy and community engagement.

  • Valjevo SECAP — May 2024: Supported the development of a coordinated framework for climate action, stronger resilience and equitable access to sustainable energy, linking environmental priorities with local economic development.

  • Vranje SECAP — May 2024: Supported the development of a plan integrating climate action, resilience and fair access to sustainable energy through inclusive participation and cooperation

items.title: EXChAngE
items.image_alt: Closing event of the project “Explore Cross-border Aquatic Biodiversity – EXChAngE” was held on 10th November 2022 at Dubrovnik University, Croatia
items.summary: Provided project management services within EXChAngE, an EU co-funded project focused on exploring cross-border aquatic biodiversity in Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Montenegro.
items.body:
Programme: IPA CBC Croatia–Bosnia and Herzegovina–Montenegro 2014–2020
Grant Agreement: HR-BA-ME419

EXChAngE strengthened cross-border tourism cooperation between Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Montenegro by connecting aquatic biodiversity with natural and cultural heritage. The project developed the Blue Pass, a joint tourism product linking thematic routes across Dubrovnik and its Aquarium, Kotor and Aquarium Boka, the Hutovo Blato Aqua Path, and Mostar’s Old Bridge and the River Neretva. Through infrastructure investment, digital services, training and coordinated promotion, it aimed to enrich visitor experiences, attract tourists and support the sustainable use of shared heritage. Led by the University of Dubrovnik, the five-partner initiative was implemented under the Interreg IPA Cross-border Cooperation Programme Croatia–Bosnia and Herzegovina–Montenegro 2014–2020, with EU co-financing from ERDF and IPA II funds.
items.contribution:
Contracted by: Institute of Marine Biology, University of Montenegro
Geographical coverage: Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro

Provided project management services within EXChAngE, an EU co-funded project focused on exploring cross-border aquatic biodiversity in Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Montenegro.

My responsibilities included:

  • Project management: Managing project implementation in accordance with the Project Subsidy Contract and Partnership Agreement, ensuring alignment with contractual obligations and agreed implementation arrangements.

  • Procurement support: Preparing technical requirements and specifications for procurement documentation and tender dossiers supporting project activities.

  • Project reporting: Preparing project reports documenting implementation progress and activities in line with contractual reporting requirements.
items.results:
• Blue Pass tourism product: Connected four thematic routes—Dubrovnik and its Aquarium, Kotor and Aquarium Boka, Hutovo Blato Aqua Path, and Mostar Aqua Path—through a joint discount voucher available at project partners’ sales points.

  • Digital visitor services: Delivered the Blue Pass–EXChAngE mobile guide for Android and iOS, covering natural and cultural heritage, thematic routes and transport information, complemented by audio guides and interactive kiosk video content.

  • Aquarium Boka improvements: Renovated the interior, installed two new aquarium tanks and improved water conditioning and conditions for marine organisms. Added an open-air exhibition with two exhibition booths and two LED information totems.

  • Dubrovnik Aquarium modernisation: Replaced three large floor tanks with modern upright acrylic tanks, improving the visitor attraction.

  • Hutovo Blato Aqua Path: Established the visitor route through vegetation clearance and waterway deepening, enabling tours during seasonal low-water conditions.

  • Mostar cultural heritage: Completed the renovation and adaptation of the City Bath “Banja” and opened the building to visitors.

  • Tourism and heritage skills: Trained more than 100 certified tourist guides through a programme addressing Adriatic Sea, Hutovo Blato and Neretva River biodiversity, alongside English-language tour presentation and project webmaster training.

  • Branding and promotional materials: Developed the Blue Pass visual identity and graphic standards, and produced promotional packs comprising eco bags, notebooks, eco pens and bookmarks.

  • Communication and outreach: Delivered dedicated project webpages, social media campaigns, a project publication, promotional videos, and opening and closing events to promote aquatic biodiversity and the cross-border tourism offer.

  • Long-term sustainability planning: Prepared the EXChAngE Action Plan for 2023–2027, defining actions, resources and implementation timelines to sustain the Blue Pass beyond project completion.

items.title: Wetland Restore
items.full_name: Ecological Network Impact Assessment for Wetland Ecosystem Revitalisation in Three Pilot Areas
items.summary: Led the ecological network impact assessment supporting wetland ecosystem revitalisation in three protected areas in Serbia: Zasavica Special Nature Reserve, Jegrička Nature Park and Bara Trskovača Protected Habitat.
items.body: WetlandRestore promoted cross-border cooperation between Croatia and Serbia to restore and protect wetland and floodplain ecosystems in the Middle Danube region. Building on earlier cooperation initiatives, the project addressed habitat degradation, biodiversity loss and gaps in knowledge and coordination through joint ecological monitoring, restoration planning for six pilot areas and small-scale restoration interventions in Zasavica, Serbia, and the Čarna sidearm, Croatia. It brought together nature conservation organisations, water management authorities and protected-area institutions to strengthen restoration capacity, engage stakeholders and raise public awareness of wetland benefits. Within this framework, the Faculty of Biology was contracted by the Nature Conservation Movement of Sremska Mitrovica to assess the impacts of proposed wetland revitalisation interventions on the ecological network in three pilot areas in Serbia.
items.contribution:
Contracted by: Faculty of Biology, University of Belgrade / Innovation Center of the Faculty of Biology
Geographical coverage: Serbia

Led the ecological network impact assessment supporting wetland ecosystem revitalisation in three protected areas in Serbia: Zasavica Special Nature Reserve, Jegrička Nature Park and Bara Trskovača Protected Habitat.

My responsibilities included:

  • Assessment coordination: Leading the expert team in conducting ecological network impact assessments for the proposed wetland revitalisation activities across the three pilot areas.

  • Study preparation: Coordinating and contributing to the preparation of three site-specific studies: the Main Ecological Network Impact Assessment for Zasavica Special Nature Reserve, Jegrička Nature Park and Bara Trskovača Protected Habitat.
items.results:
• Prepared the Main Ecological Network Impact Assessment for wetland revitalisation in Zasavica Special Nature Reserve.

  • Prepared the Main Ecological Network Impact Assessment for wetland revitalisation in Jegrička Nature Park.

  • Prepared the Main Ecological Network Impact Assessment for wetland revitalisation in Bara Trskovača Protected Habitat.

items.title: MonteAqua
items.summary: Managed the establishment of Aquarium Boka, Montenegro’s first public aquarium, with 360 m² of renovated facilities and 25 tanks holding 43,700 litres. The project also established wildlife rescue facilities and delivered conservation training and the AdriBioPro2019 international conference.
items.body: MonteAqua aimed to strengthen the conservation of marine and freshwater biodiversity in Montenegro while supporting alignment with EU nature protection requirements under Chapter 27 of the accession process. Funded by the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs through the Norwegian Embassy in Belgrade and implemented by the University of Montenegro’s Institute of Marine Biology, the project centred on establishing Aquarium Boka as a marine biodiversity conservation and education centre, alongside freshwater aquarium and wildlife rescue facilities. It combined institutional capacity building, regional cooperation, scientific assessments and public engagement to improve the management of aquatic ecosystems. Through training on EU environmental legislation, stakeholder networking, communication tools and an international conference, MonteAqua sought to strengthen conservation governance, raise awareness of aquatic biodiversity and promote sustainable resource use, contributing to Sustainable Development Goal 14.
items.contribution:
Contracted by: Institute of Marine Biology, University of Montenegro
Geographical coverage: Montenegro

As project manager, I secured successful implementation of main project activities: 

  • Setting up Marine Biodiversity Conservation Center “Boka Aquarium” in the Institute of Marine Biology in Kotor

  • Setting up freshwater “Skadar Aquarium” in National Park “Skadar lake”

  • Development of communication platform for stakeholders’ participation in water biodiversity conservation

  • Organizing capacity building workshops

  • Organization of International conference “Adriatic Biodiversity Protection” in 2019.
items.results:
• Aquarium Boka: Established Montenegro’s first public aquarium within the Adriatic Biodiversity Conservation Center at the Institute of Marine Biology, combining research, conservation and education.

  • Wildlife rescue facilities: Established a rescue centre for sea turtles and other endangered marine animals.

  • Aquarium infrastructure: Renovated 360 m² and installed 25 aquarium tanks with a combined capacity of 43,700 litres.

  • Freshwater conservation: Established the Skadar Aquarium within the visitor centre of Skadar Lake National Park.

  • Regional cooperation: Established the AdriBioPro network, connecting institutions and experts involved in aquatic ecosystem conservation.

  • International conference: Organised AdriBioPro2019 in Kotor, featuring 92 presentations, and published its Book of Abstracts.

  • Institutional capacity building: Delivered four workshops covering invasive alien species, sustainable fisheries and illegal fishing, the Zoo Directive and CITES, and the Habitats Directive.

  • Scientific and policy publications: Produced four white papers and studies addressing rare and endangered Adriatic fish, European eel in Skadar Lake, coastal and marine conservation, and marine pollution prevention.

  • Digital engagement: Developed the MonteAqua 9mCollab stakeholder platform and Aquarium Boka web portal, supported by 30 video clips and 10 interviews.

  • Long-term sustainability: Prepared Aquarium Boka’s business plan and secured its institutional integration within the Institute of Marine Biology.

items.title: WATER SUM
items.full_name: Sustainable Use of Transboundary Water Resources and Water Security Management
items.image_alt: Sustainable Use of Transboundary Water Resources and Water Security Management (WATER SUM)
items.summary: Directed a regional initiative supporting integrated water resources management, local water security and knowledge exchange in Tunisia, Egypt and Jordan.
items.body: WATER SUM addressed water-related challenges and promoted regional cooperation in the Middle East and North Africa, focusing on Tunisia, Egypt and Jordan. Implemented by the Regional Environmental Center for Central and Eastern Europe (REC) and funded by the Government of Sweden through the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida), the project combined two complementary components. WATER POrT strengthened skills and knowledge exchange in integrated water resources management to support sustainable development and climate adaptation. WaSe supported local water security action planning to help communities address resource scarcity and environment-related tensions. Through assessments, capacity building, demonstration activities and stakeholder cooperation, WATER SUM aimed to improve water governance, strengthen community resilience and address the interlinked challenges of poverty, biodiversity loss and environmental degradation. See project photo gallery on this LINK.
items.contribution:
Organization: Regional Environmental Center for Central and Eastern Europe (REC)
Geographical coverage: Middle East and North Africa — Tunisia, Egypt and Jordan

As Project Director, I provided overall quality control across WATER SUM’s water resources management and local water security components. Supervised project management and team members, monitored implementation against project objectives and planned activities, and coordinated information flow between the project team, beneficiaries and donor. Served as REC’s designated contact for Sida under Grant Agreement Contribution ID 52030234, supporting communication concerning project implementation and the donor relationship.
items.results:
• Provided overall quality control across the WATER POrT and WaSe components, supporting coordinated implementation of regional water management and local water security activities.

  • Supervised project management and team members and monitored progress against project objectives and planned activities.

  • Coordinated information exchange between the project team and beneficiaries, supporting cooperation across Tunisia, Egypt and Jordan.

  • Prepared Background document for the REC’s World Café 2016 at WWW2016 (R. Laušević, V. Vassilev, A. Kis, F. Abdulla and S. Milutinović (2016): Water, Growth and Stability. Regional Environmental Center, Szentendre, Hungary).

  • Prepared Local Water Security Action Planning Manual (R. Laušević, S. Milutinović, J. Petersen-Perlman, M. Reed, A. Graves, M. Bartula, S. Sušić, A. Popović (2016): Local Water Security Action Planning Manual. ISBN 978-963-9638-69-3. Regional Environmental Center, Szentendre, Hungary).

  • Served as REC’s designated contact for Sida under Grant Agreement Contribution ID 52030234, maintaining management-level communication between the implementing organisation and donor.

items.title: LINK
items.full_name: Local Initiatives for a Sustainable Ukraine
items.summary: Provided strategic leadership for a Norwegian-funded initiative supporting participatory local governance, energy security planning, civil society engagement and environmental education in Ukraine.
items.body:
Organization: Regional Environmental Center for Central and Eastern Europe (REC)
Geographical coverage: Ukraine

LINK supported participatory local governance, energy security and resource-efficient development in Ukraine. Implemented by the Regional Environmental Center for Central and Eastern Europe (REC) with funding from the Norwegian Ministry of Climate and Environment, the project brought together municipal authorities, civil society organisations, businesses and citizens to address local environmental and energy challenges. Its three complementary components combined local environmental and energy security planning, civil society capacity building and cooperation grants, and environmental education through a multimedia Citizens Pack. Working with partner municipalities, LINK aimed to translate community priorities into practical actions and investment opportunities while strengthening public participation, transparency and local ownership. The initiative formed part of REC’s wider framework programme for strengthening local environmental planning and environmental civil society in Ukraine.
items.contribution: As Project Director at the Regional Environmental Center for Central and Eastern Europe (REC), provided strategic direction and oversight for LINK’s implementation in Ukraine. Guided the integration of local energy security planning, civil society support and environmental education into a coordinated approach to sustainable municipal development. Supported cooperation between the project team, municipal authorities and other stakeholders, with emphasis on participatory planning, institutional commitment and the identification of local environmental and energy investment priorities. Connected LINK’s activities with REC’s broader Framework Programme for Ukraine, for which I also served as Framework Programme Director.
items.results:
• Contributed to the development of REC’s Framework Programme “Strengthening Local Environmental Planning and Environmental Civil Society in Ukraine”, connecting municipal planning and investment preparation with civil society support, environmental education and public awareness.

  • Helped define the Local Energy Security Planning approach, linking energy demand and supply with urban planning, transport, waste and water management, stakeholder participation and investment preparation.

  • Supported the formalisation of municipal cooperation through Memoranda of Understanding signed with Cherkasy, Ivano-Frankivsk and Lubny, while advancing cooperation arrangements with Poltava and Berdychiv.

  • Supported structured follow-up with all five partner municipalities during the January 2016 mission, securing renewed commitments from local administrations and agreement on next steps for planning, coordination, training and pilot project preparation.

items.title: WGS Initiative
items.image_alt: Boy jumping in irrigation canal in arid area
items.summary: Provided strategic leadership for a regional initiative connecting water governance, sustainable development and stability through stakeholder dialogue and knowledge exchange between the MENA region and Europe.
items.body: The Water, Growth and Stability Initiative emerged from the WATER SUM project to strengthen cooperation on water governance, sustainable development and stability in the Middle East and North Africa. Launched during the April 2016 stakeholder conference in Szentendre, Hungary, the initiative was supported and managed by the Regional Environmental Center for Central and Eastern Europe (REC) in cooperation with strategic partners. It brought together perspectives from government, academia, business, civil society and municipalities around three pillars: water for sustainable development; water for growth and stability; and good governance for water. The initiative envisaged a knowledge platform, an expert network linking the MENA region and Europe, and e-learning tools to support capacity building, climate adaptation and the exchange of practical experience.
items.contribution:
Organisation: Regional Environmental Center for Central and Eastern Europe (REC)
Geographical coverage: Middle East and North Africa, with cooperation and knowledge exchange involving European partners

As Project Director, provided strategic leadership for the launch and development of the WGS Initiative within the WATER SUM framework. Contributed to dialogue connecting water management, regional cooperation and sustainable development. At the founding conference, facilitated the panel on the importance of transboundary water cooperation for development, peace and stability; participated in discussions on regional approaches and future priorities; and presented within the session launching the Manual for Local Water Security Action Planning. Supported the formulation of the initiative’s objectives and arrangements for continued stakeholder cooperation.
items.results:
• Supported the launch of the WGS Initiative at the April 2016 conference in Szentendre, where participants endorsed a framework for continued cooperation on water management, sustainable development and stability.

  • Contributed to defining the initiative’s three strategic pillars: water for sustainable development; water for growth and stability; and good governance for water.

  • Helped formulate a stakeholder governance model comprising a High-Level Panel and five forums representing academia, business, civil society, municipalities and women.

  • Facilitated dialogue on the contribution of transboundary water cooperation to development, peace and stability, connecting perspectives from the MENA region and Europe.

  • Contributed to the conference launch of the Manual for Local Water Security Action Planning, linking practical planning methods with the initiative’s wider knowledge-sharing objectives.

  • Supported the formulation of priorities captured in the draft conference outcome document, including capacity building, climate adaptation, regional cooperation, resource mobilisation and development of a longer-term framework programme.

items.title: EMC

Geographical coverage: Serbia

I edited International Science Conference “Reporting for Sustainability” proceedings. Besides that publication, the main EMC project outputs are the established Environmental Management Center within Serbian Agency for Environmental Protection (SEPA) including necessary computer hardware and software, training of personnel, introducing efficient and sound routines and practices.
items.results:

  • Supported the establishment of the Environmental Management Center within the Serbian Environmental Protection Agency (SEPA), equipped with the necessary computer hardware and software.

  • Supported personnel training and the introduction of efficient working procedures and sound environmental management practices.

items.title: SEE BAP
items.full_name: Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services for Local Sustainable Development in the Western Balkans
items.image_alt: Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services for Local Sustainable Development in the Western Balkans
items.summary: Supervised REC’s contribution to biodiversity-led local development in ten Western Balkan municipalities, supporting participatory action planning, methodological development and practical conservation initiatives.
items.body: SEE BAP connected biodiversity conservation and ecosystem services with sustainable local development in ten municipalities across the Western Balkans. Funded by Finland’s Ministry for Foreign Affairs and implemented by the European Centre for Nature Conservation (ECNC) in cooperation with the Regional Environmental Center for Central and Eastern Europe (REC), the project combined municipal assessments, stakeholder engagement, training and Local Biodiversity Action Planning (LBAP). It helped communities identify conservation priorities and biodiversity-based economic opportunities, prepare action plans and implement selected local initiatives. Working across the Drina and Drin river basins, the project promoted cooperation between municipalities and linked environmental protection with local livelihoods, poverty reduction and community participation. A practical handbook and regional knowledge exchange supported wider application of the approach.
items.contribution:
Organisation: Regional Environmental Center for Central and Eastern Europe (REC), working in partnership with ECNC
Geographical coverage: Western Balkans — Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia

As REC’s Project Director, provided overall supervision of REC’s contribution, with responsibility for quality control and links with policymakers. Worked with the ECNC-led project team, REC country offices and local stakeholders to connect biodiversity conservation and ecosystem services with municipal development priorities. Edited the Local Biodiversity Action Planning methodology, contributing to a practical approach combining stakeholder participation, conservation objectives and sustainable economic opportunities. Supported coordination and quality assurance across municipal assessments, capacity building, action planning and implementation of priority biodiversity measures.
items.results:
• Edited the LBAP methodology, contributing to the practical framework presented in the published Handbook for Developing Local Biodiversity Action Plans and its supporting resources, translated into six languages.

  • Supported the development of ten Local Biodiversity Action Plans covering Bajina Bašta, Čajetina, Goražde, Srebrenica, Pljevlja, Žabljak, Peshkopi, Dragash, Gostivar and Mavrovo-Rostuša.

  • Supported municipal assessments identifying biodiversity resources, development opportunities, stakeholder needs and priority conservation issues as the evidence base for local action planning.

  • Provided oversight and quality assurance for capacity building, including two regional workshops in October 2009 and follow-up training in May 2010 involving more than 50 municipal representatives.

  • Supported municipal ownership through cooperation agreements with all ten municipalities and the appointment of local LBAP coordinators and teams.

  • Supported the financing and implementation of priority biodiversity actions, with project contributions of up to EUR 20,000 per municipality and municipal co-financing requirements. Funded activities covered species conservation, botanical and nursery gardens, river protection, nature trails, visitor information and biodiversity-based local livelihoods.

  • Contributed to regional exchange through the “Biodiversity Goes Local” conference in Budva on 13–14 October 2011, bringing together more than 95 participants and producing a conference declaration and proposals for continued municipal learning.

  • Supported dissemination of the LBAP approach through regional and international channels, including CBD COP10, the Dinaric Arc initiative and cooperation with other conservation and development organisations.

items.title: Aquatic ecosystems
items.full_name: Structure and dynamics of aquatic ecosystems of different trophic levels
items.summary: As a research team member, I contributed to hydrobiological (limnological) research of Vlasina reservoir (Serbia). My research was focused on floristical composition of algae and seasonal and spatial dynamics of phytoplankton in Vlasina reservoir.
items.body: The project investigated the structure and dynamics of aquatic ecosystems at different trophic levels in Serbia. Its hydrobiological and limnological research included Vlasina Reservoir, examining algal species composition and seasonal and spatial patterns in phytoplankton communities.
items.contribution:
Contracted by: Ministry of Science, Republic of Serbia
Geographical coverage: Serbia

As a research team member contracted by the Ministry of Science of the Republic of Serbia, contributed to hydrobiological and limnological research at Vlasina Reservoir. Focused on algal species composition and the seasonal and spatial dynamics of phytoplankton.
items.results:
• Contributed to the characterisation of algal species composition in Vlasina Reservoir.

  • Investigated seasonal changes and spatial variation in phytoplankton communities.

  • Contributed research findings to the project’s broader investigation of aquatic ecosystem structure and dynamics.
